description:
C++26 introduces std::hive, a new container designed to combine stable references and efficient erasure with better memory locality than a linked list. But where does it actually fit performance-wise compared with std::vector and std::list?

How fast is C++26’s std::hive?

by Daniel Lemire

From the article:

C++26 adds a new container to the standard library: std::hive. It is meant to occupy the ground between std::vector and std::list. Like a vector, it keeps its elements in contiguous blocks of memory, so scanning it does not require you to chase a pointer for every e
title: How fast is C++26’s std::hive? -- Daniel Lemire
